title: Face a costly choice without inventing a lossless answer

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: A tragic choice can leave a real loss after a defensible decision. Fair process does not require the disadvantaged people to endorse the outcome or feel grateful.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Two groups requested the only quiet room for Saturday 14–16: study and bereavement support. Both are eligible and applied at the same time. Posted rule: simultaneous eligible requests go to an observed lottery run by the venue coordinator. No urgency exception or alternative room/date exists today. The coordinator may accept a correction to eligibility facts before the draw. The next opening has no known date or priority arrangement.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Apply the rule, explain the decision to the group losing the draw and distinguish actual mitigation from an unconfirmed possibility. Do not presume either group’s lesser worth.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A decision maker says “the process was fair, so nobody suffered a loss.” What is missing?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: The coordinator can run the agreed lottery after checking eligibility; the losing occasion remains lost. Offer accurate future availability information when known, not invented first priority. Later fiction: study wins the draw; bereavement support receives notice but no replacement. Partial: cite fairness without naming the loss. Incorrect: invent urgency or promise the next slot. A different case could justify another process, but not by quietly rewriting this one.
criteria: The disadvantaged group’s loss remains visible

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: Process justification and remaining harm are separate. Describe the actual lost opportunity and feasible response without undoing the explanation of the decision.
criteria: The disadvantaged group’s loss remains visible
